findings.title: `getClientsWithPermission` does not find per-client resources because their resource type is never set
findings.body: `getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` queries `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However, in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(...)` (lines 104-110), when a per-client (or per-user) resource is created via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())`, `resource.setType(resourceType)` is never called (only the top-level "all-resource" resources created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init(...)` have `type` set). As a result, `findByType` will never return individual client resources, and `getClientsWithPermission` (which is used by `ClientsResource.getClients` to filter and list clients a caller has access to when they don't have global view/manage permissions) will not return the IDs of clients granted individual permissions (or will only return the literal string `"Clients"` if an all-clients permission is granted, which is not a valid client ID). Notice that `PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient` only passed `clients().findAll()` because `myclient` was given `MANAGE`, which makes `canConfigure(myclient)` -> `canView(myclient)` return true when iterating, whereas `ClientsResource` relies on `getClientsWithPermission` for filtering when listing.

findings.title: `getResourceName` does not handle `CLIENTS` resource type
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` (lines 304-326) only resolves human-readable names for `USERS.getType()` (returning `"All users"` or `user.getUsername()`) and falls back to `resource.getDisplayName()` for other resource types. For `CLIENTS` resources, `displayName` is not set, so representations of client permissions/resources (e.g., in the Admin UI / REST API policy resource list) will return `null` (or the internal UUID) instead of `"All clients"` or the client's `clientId`.

findings.title: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` ignores the "all-clients" permission when a per-client resource exists for a different scope
findings.body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)` (lines 214-234), if a resource for `client.getId()` exists in `resourceStore` (for example, because a permission was created on that specific client for `VIEW`), `resource` is non-null, so the fallback to the `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` ("all-clients") resource in lines 215-222 is skipped completely. If the caller was granted `MANAGE` on "all-clients" and a separate permission exists on `client` for `VIEW` (or for another user), evaluating `hasPermission(client, MANAGE)` will only evaluate permissions attached to the specific client resource and will return `false`, failing to fall back to the "all-clients" permission (unlike `UserPermissionsV2`, which evaluates both the user resource and the all-users resource).
